sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue up 35% YoY, core loss per share improved from ($2.90) to ($1.24), and free cash flow improved from ($4.3B) to ($0.2B). Management explicitly raised the free cash flow outlook for the full year to approximately ($3B), better than prior expectations, and expressed confidence in positive Q4 free cash flow. However, structural risks remain, including the ongoing 737-7/10 certification delay to 2026 and a potential $700M DOJ payment, which prevent a higher score.

summary.revenue: $22.7 billion, up 35% from $16.9 billion in Q2 2024, primarily reflecting 150 commercial deliveries.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.92) and core loss per share (non-GAAP) of ($1.24), improved from ($2.33) and ($2.90) respectively in Q2 2024.
summary.guidance: Full-year free cash flow expected to be approximately ($3B), with Q3 free cash flow similar to Q2 usage and Q4 positive. 737 deliveries expected to be slightly above 400 for the year. 787 deliveries at the high end of 70-80 range. BCA margins expected to remain negative for the year but improving each quarter.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of (0.8)% improved from (6.5)% in Q2 2024. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of (1.9)% improved from (8.3)%. BCA operating margin (5.1)% improved from (11.9)%. BDS operating margin 1.7% improved from (15.2)%. BGS operating margin 19.9% improved from 17.8%.
key_risks: 737-7 and 737-10 certification delayed to 2026 due to engine anti-ice solution taking longer than expected.
Potential $700 million one-time payment related to DOJ non-prosecution agreement in Q3.
Dynamic global trade environment with ongoing tariff risks, particularly regarding China and USMCA.
Work stoppage risk from strike at BDS facilities in St. Louis and St. Charles (approximately 3,200 employees).
Fixed-price development programs still in progress, representing 15% of BDS revenue.
key_opportunities: Strong market demand with backlog of $619 billion, including over 5,900 commercial airplanes.
737 production rate increased to 38 per month with plan to request FAA approval for 42 per month in coming months.
787 production rate now at 7 per month with KPIs all green, preparing for future rate increases.
BDS captured $19B in orders in the quarter, including $2.8B Space Force contract.
Recent trade deals (EU, UK, Japan) expected to reduce tariff impacts, potentially beating the $500M input tariff bogey.
Reconciliation Bill increases national defense spending by $150B through FY2029, benefiting Boeing defense programs.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management uses language like 'our recovery plan is taking hold,' 'we're starting to see real momentum,' and 'I'm pleased with our progress' while acknowledging remaining work, indicating confidence in the trajectory.
